the amount of free wireless bandwidth is the main parameter that affects the quality of Voip calls in 802.1lb WLANs.
the resource usage at the MAC layer is a strong predictor of the call quality of VoIP traffic over 802.11 WLANs.
the resource utilization at the MAC layer can be a very good indicator of VoIP call performance in terms of delay, jitter, loss, and thus user satisfaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a strong correlation between resource utilization and call quality.
the resource utilization is a useful indicator of the quality of Voip calls in WLANs.
the quality of Voip calls is strongly correlated with the available bandwidth, and the correlation is stronger when the call is under congestion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of free MAC bandwidth is an excellent predictor of VoIP quality.
the amount of free wireless bandwidth is a very strong indicator of the quality of VoIp calls in 802. 11b WLANs, with the exception of very low and very high bandwidth utilization scenarios.
